Blocks.Text: As LinkedIn partners, you can upload and sync attachments, enabling recruiters to access these materials directly within your ATS systems. You can link documents to job applications.
The following sections explain two main workflows for managing candidate documents in LinkedIn:

Upload resume: A two-step process where you first request a signed URL from LinkedIn, then upload the resume file directly to that URL.

Sync application resume: Use this API to link uploaded documents to applications or candidate profiles in LinkedIn.
Note
The latest API version is 202604. Use this version in the LinkedIn-Version header for all API requests to access the most recent features and improvements.
To upload a resume, you first need to get a signed URL from LinkedIn and then use it to upload the file.
When uploading a resume, consider the following guidelines:

Use one of the supported media formats from PDF, DOC, DOCX, or TXT.
Ensure that the media file size does not exceed 10MB for all file types.
Upload only one resume object per API call.
Ensure that all calls to upload a resume use OAuth 2.0 authentication.
Take the following steps to upload a resume:

1.1 Create URL
1.2 Upload resume file
Use the following endpoint to create a URL:
POST https://api.linkedin.com/v2/hireMediaUrl

This API is governed by OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework and you must pass a bearer access token in your request as authorization header. Obtain access tokens via OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow. Use your customer's application client_id and client_secret to obtain the access token.

Rows.Text: This helps LinkedIn to uniquely identify the use case for which media upload is being done. For this use case, refer to the value as shown in the sample request below.

The type of the resume file. Valid values are: "text/plain" for TXT file"application/pdf" for PDF file"application/msword" for DOC file"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document" for DOCX file
The name of the resume file.
The contract which is signed by the customer with LinkedIn to use LinkedIn Recruiter services. Must be in the format urn:li:contract:{Id}.
ENUM values of the type: MILLISECOND, SECOND, MINUTE, HOUR, DAY, WEEK, MONTH, YEAR

Blocks.Text: Headers:

Authorization: Bearer {token}
Accept:application/json
Content-Type:application/json
X-RestLi-Protocol-Version:2.0.0
A successful request returns a 201 HTTP response code. The response has an empty body and contains a signed URL in the x-linkedin-id response header.

HTTP/2 201 
x-li-responseorigin: RGW
location: /hireMediaUrl/https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fambry%2F%3Fx-li-ambry-ep=IKNzqXRAxc1n6yCEaLQFyikjNuvufa9i6Ek2Or5V4RpUZu8AY9CRylnLjOWX6ABe05uiXOyr0rw6hvnNcDdJLEd1Kunfn...fdfr67h
x-linkedin-id: https://www.linkedin.com/ambry/?x-li-ambry-ep=IKNzqXRAxc1n6yCEaLQFyikjNuvufa9i6Ek2Or5V4RpUZu8AY9CRylnLjOWX6ABe05uiXOyr0rw6hvnNcDdJLEd1Kunfn...fdfr67h
x-restli-protocol-version: 2.0.0
content-length: 0
date: Thu, 17 Jun 2021 09:27:30 GMT
After getting a signed URL, upload the resume file by calling the following API. This API expects the Content-Type header. The valid values are:

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer {token}" -H 'Content-Type: application/pdf' https://www.linkedin.com/ambry/?x-li-ambry-ep=AQEvzZSZZQH75QAAAXhws9LWCtrppkjlS2oJyQOrJA...1XFGyS1XfEvSo --data-binary @datafile
A successful request returns a 201 HTTP response code. The response has an empty body and contains file location in the location response header.

HTTP/2 201 
cache-control: no-cache, no-store
pragma: no-cache
expires: Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
location: /AAYUAgCvAAkAAQAAAAJFyLgwRkz_TmebRMrAixANdQ.txt
x-li-uuid: HP2pABxWiRI1FsAisAAA==
date: Thu, 17 Jun 2021 09:56:58 GMT
content-length: 0
Sync uploaded candidate documents with their applications or profiles. Use the following endpoint after uploading files to ensure recruiters can access the documents.
PUT https://api.linkedin.com/rest/attachments

Rows.Text: The unique ID assigned by the external system to the parent entity.
The unique identifier for the attachment assigned by the external provider.
This specifies who owns the attachment. The format is "urn:li:organization:{id}".
The type of the external reference entity. The available option is APPLICATION.
The type of the attachment. The available option is RESUME.
The original file name of the attachment as provided by your system.
The file format of the uploaded document (for example, PDF, DOCX).

The internal URN of the file record within LinkedIn's storage systems. This represents the Ambry URN returned by LinkedIn (for example, urn:li:ambryBlob:AYEBADqAAkAAQAAAAAAAS7h6TEbMXRJQQ2DTaGESDnzow.pdf).
The timestamp when the file was created in your system (epoch milliseconds, UTC). It must be a positive value and not a future timestamp.
The timestamp when the file was last modified in your system (epoch milliseconds, UTC). It must be a positive value and not a future timestamp.

Blocks.Text: Note

The externalReferenceEntityType field currently only supports "APPLICATION".
The attachmentType field currently only supports "RESUME".
Supported file types for attachments:

Rows.Text: This represents a Microsoft Word document (.doc).
This represents a Microsoft Word document (.docx).
This represents a plain text file.

Blocks.Text: The type of entity the attachment is associated with:

Rows.Text: The job application that the attachment is associated with.

Blocks.Text: The type of attachment being synced:

Rows.Text: This represents a resume or CV document.

--header 'x-restli-method: batch_update' \
--header 'LinkedIn-Version: 202508' \
--header 'Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=xyz' \
--header 'X-HTTP-Method-Override: PUT' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {token}' \
--data '--xyz
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

--xyz
